summary: Tanzan Ishibashi (1884–1973) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kofu Daiichi High School and Waseda University (~1903–1907), he worked at Yokohama Mainichi Shimbun (~1908–1911), Toyo Keizai (~1911–1946), and Rissho University (~1952–1968).

Tao Jiang works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo, also studying under Ellen Y. Zhang, Kathleen Uno, Charles Wei-hsun Fu, and Nathan Sivin, and held an associate professorship at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under the supervision of Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed a BA at Fudan University (2010) and earned a Magister Artium at the University of Munich.
Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1962–1999) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1967–1999).

Tarthang Tulku (b. 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, having studied under Agyur Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima, and Jampel Gyepai Dorje. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and founded the Nyingma Institute.

Taryo Makita (1912–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, studying at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities. He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1957–1976) and later served as president and executive director at Saitama Institute of Technology (1997, 2001).

Tashi Tsering (b. 1960) works in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated under numerous teachers including Tenzin Gyatso, he served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979), founded the Amnye Machen Institute (~1992), and taught at CIHTS (attested 2014–2019).

Tatiana Oranskaia (b. 1950) specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1973) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (~1987–1988), holding positions at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato (b. 1924) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Komazawa University in 1978. He held academic positions at Komazawa University (attested 1972–1978, 1994), Ryukoku University (attested 1974), and Tokai University.
Tatsuhiro Saito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Tatsuo Hayashi (1896–1984) was a scholar in philosophy and history/archaeology who studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1921). He held positions at Hosei University (~1926–1930), Toyo University (~1928–1932), Tsuda University (~1932–1968), Meiji University, and Rikkyo University.

Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) studied linguistics, Tibetology, and sinology at Kyoto University, earning a doctorate in 1962. He spent his career at Kyoto University (1956–1992), including serving as professor and dean, before posts at NACSIS (1992–1994) and Toyo Bunko (1997).

Tatsushi Tamai is a scholar in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts as a visiting researcher at Soka University (attested 2013) and its International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (attested 2010–2016).

Tatyana Elizarenkova (1929–2007) worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Mikhaïl Peterson at Moscow State University (~1946–1951) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1957–2007).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat (b. 1950) studied under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho and at the University of Hawaiʻi. He held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013) in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy.
Taw Sein Ko (1864–1930) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1881–1882) and later at the Inner Temple and Inns of Court (~1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga (1915–1983) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1938), he held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1946–1947), the University of Tokyo (~1947–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma (b. 1941) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Banaras Hindu University (~1965–1968) and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.
